The steal effect moves one aura token from the attacker's arena to your control. Steal Victory is not an action card — it is a block card (similar to a defense reaction but played from hand freely during the defend step). It has 3 defense.
Can Steal Victory's steal effect fire if the attacking hero has no aura tokens?

If the attacking hero controls no aura tokens when Steal Victory's trigger resolves, the steal effect does nothing — there is nothing to steal. The trigger still fires when Steal Victory defends, but it has no legal target and the effect fails silently. Steal Victory still provides its 3 defense regardless.
What is a Sigil in Flesh and Blood?

A Sigil is an Aura card type that typically has the word 'Sigil' in its name. Sigils enter the arena when played and remain there until their leave-the-arena trigger fires. Most Sigils are Instant Auras: they are destroyed at the beginning of your action phase, and when they leave the arena, they produce an effect. Some Sigils have additional static effects while in the arena (like Sigil of Conductivity's Arcane Shelter 1).
When does a Sigil's on-leave effect trigger?

A Sigil's 'when this leaves the arena' trigger fires whenever the Sigil exits any arena zone for any reason — whether destroyed by its own start-of-action-phase trigger, targeted by an enemy effect, or bounced to hand. The trigger fires upon departure from the arena, not just upon destruction, so returning a Sigil to hand also triggers its leave effect.
What does Sigil of Aether do when it leaves the arena?

When Sigil of Aether leaves the arena, it deals 1 arcane damage to any target. If damage is dealt, it also triggers Amp 1, increasing the arcane damage of the next arcane damage source this turn by 1. Sigil of Aether is a Wizard Instant Aura that is destroyed at the beginning of your action phase, which immediately triggers the on-leave effect.
What is the difference between Sigil of Aether and Sigil of Brilliance?

Both Sigils are Wizard Instant Auras destroyed at the start of your action phase. Sigil of Aether deals 1 arcane damage to any target and amps 1 when it leaves. Sigil of Brilliance draws a card when it leaves. Sigil of Brilliance also has Oscilio Specialization, meaning it can only be included in decks helmed by Oscilio. Sigil of Aether has no class restriction.
What does Sigil of Brilliance do when it leaves the arena?

Sigil of Brilliance draws a card for its controller when it leaves the arena. It is a Lightning Wizard Instant Aura with Oscilio Specialization. It is destroyed at the beginning of your action phase, which immediately triggers the card-draw. Because it is a Lightning-type card, playing it also records 'played_lightning' for effects like Volzar the Lightning Rod's Amp X calculation.
What does Sigil of Conductivity do, and how is it different from Sigil of Aether?

Sigil of Conductivity is a Lightning Instant Aura with Arcane Shelter 1. While it is in your arena, Arcane Shelter 1 reduces the first arcane damage you would be dealt each turn by 1. When Sigil of Conductivity leaves the arena for any reason, you create an Embodiment of Lightning token. Unlike Sigil of Aether, it has no action-phase destruction trigger — it persists until destroyed by an external effect.
Does a Sigil create its token if it is bounced back to hand rather than destroyed?

Yes. The 'when this leaves the arena' trigger fires for any reason the Sigil exits the arena, including being returned to hand. If Sigil of Conductivity is bounced to hand, it still creates an Embodiment of Lightning token because it left the arena zone. The trigger is not conditional on destruction — departure from any arena zone is sufficient.
What does Sigil of Catharsis refer to in the card pool?

Sigil of Catharsis is not among the Sigils implemented in this simulator's database. The implemented Sigils in this engine include Sigil of Aether, Sigil of Brilliance, Sigil of Conductivity, Sigil of Cycles, Sigil of Deadwood, Sigil of Earth, Sigil of Forethought, Sigil of Fyendal, Sigil of Lightning, Sigil of Parapets, Sigil of Permafrost, Sigil of Protection, Sigil of Sanctuary, Sigil of Shelter, and Sigil of Solace. You may be thinking of one of these or a card from a set not yet in the database.
What does Sigil of Solace do?

Sigil of Solace is a card registered in the engine with a simple on-play trigger: when played, you gain 3 life. It is categorized as an Instant in the triggers registry. Unlike most Sigils that have Aura in their type and a leave-the-arena effect, Sigil of Solace functions more as a direct life-gain instant effect when played. The engine implements it via the CARD_TRIGGERS on_play event.
What does Sigil of Lightning do when it leaves the arena?

Sigil of Lightning creates an Embodiment of Lightning token when it leaves the arena. It is destroyed at the beginning of your action phase (like most Wizard Instant Aura Sigils), which immediately triggers the token creation. The Embodiment of Lightning can then be used with cards that interact with it, such as Channel Lightning Valley or Volzar the Lightning Rod effects.
How are Harpoon weapons different from other weapon attacks?

Harpoon weapons in this engine (Red Fin Harpoon, Blue Fin Harpoon, Yellow Fin Harpoon, King Shark Harpoon, King Kraken Harpoon, Goldfin Harpoon) have on-hit triggered effects. When a harpoon hits a hero, the defending hero chooses (or reveals) a card from their hand; if that card meets the harpoon's condition, it is discarded and you create a Gold token. The condition varies by harpoon: Red Fin checks for red cards, Blue Fin for blue cards, Yellow Fin for yellow cards, King Shark for attack action cards, and King Kraken for non-attack action cards.
When does a harpoon's Go Fish trigger fire?

The harpoon's on-hit effect (called the 'Go Fish' pattern internally) fires on the 'hit' event — after the attack resolves and damage is dealt to the defending hero. If the harpoon does not hit (the attack is fully blocked), the trigger does not fire. The trigger requires the attack to deal at least 1 damage to the hero to count as a hit.
What happens if the Hammerhead Harpoon Cannon activates before a harpoon attack?

When you activate the Hammerhead Harpoon Cannon by paying 4 resources and tapping it, your next arrow attack gets +4 power, and if that next arrow attack is a harpoon, it also gains Overpower. The activation also gives you an action point (Go again). The 'activated_cannon' flag is also set, which enables certain conditional harpoon effects like Shallow Water Shark Harpoon's on-hit arsenal destruction and the cannon-mode of the Go Fish variants (allowing you to look at the hand rather than the opponent choosing).
What is the difference in how pistol-type versus dagger-type weapons work in this engine?

In this engine, dagger-type cards (both weapons and action cards with the Dagger subtype) receive buff effects from a shared dagger-buff listener registered on the 'attacking' event. Pistol-type weapons are not specifically implemented as a distinct category in the current card pool. Daggers benefit from effects like Up Sticks and Run, Savor Bloodshed, Cut from the Same Cloth, and the Graphene Chelicera stealth-dagger buff. These buffs are consumed when the next dagger attack declares.
Can a dagger-type action card (like Kiss of Death) receive dagger buffs from cards like Savor Bloodshed?

Yes. In this engine, dagger buffs apply to any card with 'Dagger' in its types list, including dagger-type action cards like Kiss of Death as well as weapon daggers. Savor Bloodshed's '+4 power to your next dagger attack' effect applies to the next attack with a Dagger type, regardless of whether it is a weapon attack or a played attack action card.
When dual wielding two weapons, which one attacks first?

In Flesh and Blood, weapon attacks are performed as Action-speed activations during your action phase. You choose which weapon to attack with each time you spend an action point and pay the weapon's attack cost. There is no fixed order — you freely choose which weapon to activate for each attack action. The engine handles each weapon attack independently as a declared action.
What is the key difference between a weapon attack and an attack action card?

A weapon attack originates from an equipped weapon card in your weapon zone using a weapon activation (typically 'Once per Turn Action' or similar). An attack action card is a card played from hand, arsenal, or the banish zone with types including Attack and Action. Weapon attacks use the weapon's power, have their own keywords, and do not typically go to the graveyard after attacking (the weapon stays equipped). Attack action cards go to the graveyard after resolving unless another effect redirects them.
Can you defend with a weapon?

No. Weapons cannot be used to defend attacks — only cards from your hand or arsenal can be played to defend (as attack action cards or defense reactions). Equipment in armor slots also provides passive defense values when not used as blockers. However, cards that happen to be weapons with types like Dagger and Action can sometimes interact with combat rules in special ways, but they do not block in the traditional sense.
What does Electrostatic Discharge do and which versions are in the database?

Electrostatic Discharge is a Lightning Instant with no cost. All three versions give the next attack action card you play this turn with cost 1 or less a power bonus: the red version (pitch 1) gives +3 power, the yellow version (pitch 2) gives +2 power, and the blue version (pitch 3) gives +1 power. It is a Lightning-type card, so playing it also counts as a 'played_lightning' event, which feeds into effects like Volzar the Lightning Rod's Amp X calculation. Note: the engine has a known bug where the electrostatic_next_attack bonus flag is never consumed by TURN_ATTACK_EFFECTS, so the power boost silently does nothing in the current implementation.
What is the Etchings of Arcana surge condition on the yellow version?

The yellow Etchings of Arcana deals 2 arcane damage and has a Surge condition: if this deals more than 2 damage (i.e., 3 or more damage after reductions), you may return an aura with Sigil in its name from your graveyard to your hand. Surge checks at damage resolution — if the final damage dealt exceeds the threshold, the surge effect fires. In the engine the surge threshold is checked at >= 3 damage dealt.
How does the Etchings of Arcana + Volzar combo work?

The combo works in two steps. First, you play a Sigil to gain its effect and have it in your arena. Second, you activate Volzar the Lightning Rod, which Amps X where X equals the number of Lightning cards you've played this turn. A Sigil played earlier in the turn (if it is a Lightning type, like Sigil of Brilliance) contributes to that count. Then Etchings of Arcana deals 2 arcane damage, which is amplified by any active Amp counters — if the resulting damage exceeds 2, the Surge fires and returns a Sigil from graveyard to hand, ready to replay.
What does Mind Warp's Surge effect do?

Mind Warp deals 2 arcane damage and has Surge: if this deals more than 2 damage to a hero (3 or more), the target hero shuffles their hand into their deck, then draws that many cards minus 1. So if they had 4 cards in hand, they shuffle all 4 in and draw 3. This can significantly disrupt an opponent's hand quality while reducing their hand size by 1. The engine checks surge at >= 3 damage dealt.
What does Channel Lightning Valley do each turn while it is in the arena?

Channel Lightning Valley is a Lightning Instant Aura. While it is in the arena, the first time you deal damage to an opposing hero each turn, you draw a card. At the beginning of your end phase, the Channel Lightning upkeep fires: you add a flow counter to it, then it is destroyed unless you put a Lightning card from your pitch zone on the bottom of your deck for each flow counter on it. So each turn it survives costs one more Lightning card from your pitch zone.
What happens if Channel Lightning Valley is in the arena but you have no Lightning cards in your pitch zone at end phase?

If Channel Lightning Valley's end-phase upkeep fires and you cannot pay the cost (one Lightning card from pitch per flow counter), Channel Lightning Valley is destroyed. The trigger adds a flow counter first, then checks if you can pay — if you cannot pay the full amount (one Lightning per counter), the card is destroyed and goes to the graveyard.
What does Blast to Oblivion do when it attacks?

When Blast to Oblivion attacks, it sets a flag that allows the next instant played this chain link to optionally return one of two targets to its owner's hand: either a target aura permanent with cost 1 or less, or a target aura token (tokens have no cost restriction for this effect). This bounce effect is consumed by the first instant played after Blast to Oblivion attacks on that chain link. Note that the card says 'owner's hand,' not necessarily your own hand — so you could target an opponent's aura token. The effect is part of Oscilio's kit and is designed to retrieve low-cost Sigil auras back to hand mid-combat for replaying. Note: in the current engine implementation, this flag is set but never read, so the bounce silently does nothing.
What does Gone in a Flash do when it attacks?

When Gone in a Flash attacks, it sets a flag that allows the next instant played this chain link to return Gone in a Flash itself from the graveyard back to hand. After Gone in a Flash goes to the graveyard post-attack, playing an instant retrieves it. This allows Gone in a Flash to be recycled and replayed multiple times in a single turn, provided you can keep playing instants.
What does Schism of Chaos do when it is pitched?

Schism of Chaos is a Chaos Resource Gem with Legendary. When it is pitched (used as a resource to pay a cost), each hero shuffles their deck, then puts the top card of their deck face-down into their arsenal, provided their arsenal is empty. This fires as a triggered ability on the card_pitched event. The effect applies to all players — both the Schism player and each opponent get the arsenal effect if their arsenal is empty.
Can Schism of Chaos be used as a regular pitch card like any other resource?

Yes. Schism of Chaos is pitched like any other resource card (placed into the pitch zone to generate resources equal to its pitch value). It has pitch value 3 (blue). The difference is that pitching it triggers its effect: each hero shuffles and places the top card of their deck into their empty arsenal. This makes pitching Schism of Chaos a significant game event beyond just generating 3 resources.
What does Riches of Trōpal-Dhani do when pitched?

Riches of Trōpal-Dhani is a Generic Resource Gem with Legendary. When it is pitched, the player who pitched it creates a Gold token. This fires as a triggered ability on the card_pitched event — the pitcher_id from the event is used to create the Gold token under the correct player's control. It has pitch value 2 (yellow).
What is a Gold token and what can it be used for?

A Gold token is a token item created by various pirate/treasure-themed cards (Crown of Dominion, Riches of Trōpal-Dhani, harpoon on-hits, etc.). Gold tokens are used as a resource or cost for certain card effects. For example, Marlynn's hero ability requires destroying a Gold token as part of its cost. Gold tokens can also be stolen by effects like the Gold-Baited Hook. They exist in the items zone while in play.
What does Zen State do as an aura token?

Zen State is a Ninja Token Aura. It enters the arena with 1 balance counter. At the beginning of your action phase, you must remove a balance counter from it or it is destroyed. While it exists, it continuously prevents 1 damage from each source that would deal damage to your hero. This is a replacement effect — each time you would take damage, 1 of that damage is prevented. Zen State is a powerful defensive token for Ninja heroes.
How long does Zen State's damage prevention last?

Zen State's damage prevention is active while it remains in the arena. It enters with 1 balance counter and is destroyed at the beginning of your action phase if you cannot or do not remove a counter. Since it starts with only 1 counter, it naturally survives for just one action phase — after that it is destroyed at the next action phase start unless somehow given more counters. While it is alive, every source of damage is reduced by 1.
What does Spellbane Aegis do as a token aura?

Spellbane Aegis is a Generic Token Aura with Spellvoid 1. Spellvoid 1 is a keyword that reduces the first arcane damage you would be dealt each turn by 1, provided you destroy this card as part of the prevention. This means Spellbane Aegis can prevent up to 1 arcane damage once — after activating Spellvoid, it is destroyed. It provides one-time arcane damage protection.
What is the difference between Arcane Barrier and Spellvoid?

Arcane Barrier N allows you to pay up to N resources to prevent that much arcane damage — it is a resource payment prevention and does not destroy the equipment. Spellvoid N is a triggered destruction: the first time you would be dealt arcane damage each turn, you may destroy this card to prevent N of that arcane damage — no resource cost required, but the card is destroyed. Arcane Barrier is on equipment like Arcanite Skullcap; Spellvoid is on tokens like Spellbane Aegis and equipment like Spell Fray pieces.
What does Spectral Shield do as an aura token?

Spectral Shield is an Illusionist Token Aura with Ward 1. Ward 1 means the first time your hero would be dealt damage from a source each turn, prevent 1 of that damage. Ward functions as a damage reduction that is always active — it does not consume the card to activate. Spectral Shield persists as long as it is in the arena, providing 1 prevention per damage instance per turn.
How is Ward different from Spellvoid on aura tokens?

Ward N passively prevents N damage from each source once per turn without destroying the card — it triggers automatically and the token survives. Spellvoid N requires you to destroy the card to prevent N arcane damage, so it is a one-time use. Ward provides ongoing protection each turn, while Spellvoid provides a single-use prevention that eliminates the token. Ward applies to all damage types; Spellvoid only prevents arcane damage.
What does Aether Ashwing do as a token ally?

Aether Ashwing is a Draconic Illusionist Token Dragon Ally with Arcane Barrier 1. As an ally, it has 1 power and 1 health and can attack. Its Arcane Barrier 1 allows you to pay 1 resource to prevent 1 arcane damage that would be dealt to you. Unlike aura tokens, Aether Ashwing is an ally — it can be targeted by attacks and effects that affect allies, and it can be destroyed by combat damage.
What happens to an aura when it is destroyed?

When an aura is destroyed, it is moved to the graveyard. If the aura has a 'when this leaves the arena' trigger, that trigger fires as the card moves out of the aura zone. The 'card_destroyed' event is also emitted after the move. Auras with leave-the-arena effects (like Sigil of Aether or Sigil of Conductivity) will produce their effects on destruction, whether it is the scheduled action-phase destruction or destruction by an external effect.
Do aura effects become active immediately when the aura enters the arena, or on the next turn?

Aura effects that are continuous static abilities (like Frailty's -1 power penalty, or Ward's damage prevention) become active immediately when the aura enters the arena. There is no delay until the next turn. Triggered abilities on auras (like 'at the beginning of your action phase') fire at the next applicable game event. So Frailty's -1 power effect applies to the very next qualifying attack after it enters, and a Sigil's action-phase destruction fires at the start of the very next action phase.
Can an aura in the arena defend an attack?

No. Aura cards in the arena cannot be used to defend attacks. Only cards from your hand or arsenal are played to defend. Aura permanents in the aura zone are passive — they provide continuous or triggered effects but cannot be selected as defenders. If an aura has a defense value printed on it (like Sigil of Cycles with 2 defense), that value may be used in other contexts such as equipment defense, but not for blocking since auras do not go to the blocking step.
What does Oscilio's hero ability do?

Oscilio (both young and adult forms) has a Once per Turn Instant ability: discard an instant from your hand as the cost, then draw a card. This is a hand-cycle ability — you trade one instant for a fresh draw. The ability is registered in HERO_ACTIVATION_CONDITIONS and requires at least one instant in hand. It can only be used once per turn and is available at instant speed.
When does Oscilio's on-play tracker fire for Lightning cards?

Oscilio's tracking trigger fires on every 'on_play' event. When a card is played, the trigger checks if it is a Lightning-type card. If so, it appends 'played_lightning' to Oscilio's current_turn_effects list. This counter accumulates throughout the turn and is used by Volzar the Lightning Rod's Amp X calculation at activation time — the more Lightning cards played that turn, the more arcane damage is amplified.
What is Flittering Charge and when does it get go again?

Flittering Charge is a card that gets go again when played if an instant has been played this chain link before it. It checks the 'played_instant_this_link' flag in the controller's current_turn_effects at the time it is played. If that flag is present (an instant was played earlier on the same chain link), Flittering Charge gains go again, granting an action point on resolution. This enables instant-to-attack combos.
What does Current Funnel do when played?

Current Funnel checks if the last card played was a Lightning-type card ('played_lightning' flag). If so, Current Funnel itself gets go again, and the next non-instant action card you play this turn also gets go again. The go again for Current Funnel is added to its keywords immediately, and a 'current_funnel_next_go_again' flag is set for the next qualifying card. This rewards chaining Lightning cards.
What does Aether Bindings of the Third Age do as equipment?

Aether Bindings of the Third Age is a Wizard Arms Equipment with Battleworn. Its Instant activated ability destroys this equipment as cost, then until end of turn, whenever a Sigil aura you control leaves the arena, amp 1. This effect is tracked via the 'aether_bindings_sigil_amp' flag. Each time a Sigil departs the arena after activation, you gain 1 Amp, increasing arcane damage for the remainder of the turn.
What does Volzar the Lightning Rod's Once per Turn Instant do?

Volzar the Lightning Rod has a Once per Turn Instant ability that costs 1 resource (or 0 if you control a Sigil aura): Amp X, where X equals the number of Lightning cards you have played this turn. This scales with your Lightning-card plays — the more Lightning cards you have played, the larger the amp. The weapon also tracks 'volzar_used' to enforce the once-per-turn restriction.
What does Amp do in Flesh and Blood?

Amp N adds N to the arcane damage of the next arcane damage source you play or activate this turn. Amp counters accumulate and are applied when arcane damage is dealt — they are consumed at that point. If you have Amp 3 and deal 2 arcane damage, the source deals 5 arcane damage total and the Amp counter is consumed. Multiple Amp effects stack their counters.
What does Schism of Chaos's effect do if both players have full arsenals?

If a player's arsenal is already full (contains a card) when Schism of Chaos's pitch trigger fires, that player cannot place the top card of their deck into their arsenal. The effect only applies if the arsenal is empty. If both players have full arsenals, neither player shuffles or places a card — the trigger fires but the effect has no valid targets and simply does nothing for those players.
How does Arakni, Marionette's hero ability interact with stealth attacks?

While in Arakni, Marionette form, stealth attacks you control that are attacking a marked hero get +1 power and gain the conditional ability 'when this hits, gain go again.' The +1 power is added via a base_power effect when the attacking event fires. The go again is granted only on hit — if the attack misses (is fully blocked), go again is not granted, and the 'arakni_stealth_hit_go_again' flag is cleaned up at combat chain close.
What is Arakni's end-phase transformation mechanic?

At the beginning of Arakni's end phase: if currently in demi-hero (Agent of Chaos) form, Arakni returns to Arakni, Marionette form ('return to the brood'). If currently in Marionette form and the opponent is marked, Arakni randomly transforms into one of the six Agent of Chaos demi-hero forms (Black Widow, Funnel Web, Orbweaver, Redback, Tarantula, or Trapdoor). This cycle repeats each turn.
What is the Mark keyword and how does it interact with Arakni's cards?

Mark is an effect keyword that marks a hero. A marked hero has the marked status, which several Arakni cards check. While marked, they may take extra effects on hit (Mark of the Black Widow forces a hand banish), stealth attacks versus them gain +1 power and go-again from Arakni's hero ability, To the Point gives a bigger bonus, and Arakni transforms into an Agent of Chaos at end phase. Mark is removed at the start of the marked player's turn.
What does Mask of Deceit do when it defends?

When Mask of Deceit defends, Arakni transforms into a randomly chosen Agent of Chaos demi-hero. If the attacking hero is marked at the time of the trigger, Arakni's player chooses which Agent of Chaos to become instead of it being random. The transformation changes the hero's slug, name, and types in place, giving access to that Agent of Chaos's abilities.
What does Blacktek Whisperers do as an Attack Reaction?

Blacktek Whisperers is a Legs Equipment with an Attack Reaction ability. The cost is destroying Blacktek Whisperers itself. The effect makes the target Assassin attack gain 'on hit, this gets go again.' The attack reaction can only be played in response to an Assassin attack. This allows an Assassin attack to gain go again after hitting, enabling another card play. The whisperers are then destroyed as the cost.
How can Blacktek Whisperers be re-equipped after being destroyed?

At the start of your turn, if Blacktek Whisperers is in your graveyard and you control at least 2 Silver tokens, you may optionally destroy 2 Silver tokens to re-equip Blacktek Whisperers from your graveyard into your legs equipment slot. This allows repeated use across turns if you can generate Silver tokens from effects like Leave No Witnesses.
What does Leave No Witnesses do on hit?

When Leave No Witnesses hits a hero, it banishes the top card of their deck. You may also banish up to 1 card from their arsenal. Leave No Witnesses also has a Contract ability: it is contracted to banish the opponent's red cards. Whenever you banish an opponent's red card while this contract is active, you create a Silver token. The contract deactivates when the combat chain closes.
What does Pain in the Backside do on hit?

When Pain in the Backside hits a hero, you choose a dagger you control (from your weapon zone or on the combat chain) and that dagger deals 1 damage to the defending hero. This is an additional damage effect triggered by the hit. If you control no daggers at the time of the trigger resolution, nothing happens. You choose which dagger if you have multiple.
What does Kiss of Death do when it hits?

Kiss of Death is a Dagger-type action card. When it hits a hero, they lose 1 life (damage that bypasses normal combat damage calculation). It also receives all applicable dagger buffs from turn-effects when it attacks, since it has Dagger in its types. Kiss of Death is a key combo piece for Arakni-style decks that stack dagger power-up effects.
What does Hunter's Klaive do when it hits?

Hunter's Klaive is a dagger weapon with Piercing 1. When it hits a hero, it marks them (applies the marked status). This synergizes heavily with Arakni's deck: marking the hero enables Arakni's stealth attack buffs, To the Point's enhanced bonus, Take Up the Mantle's copy effect, and triggers Arakni's end-phase transformation.
What does Savor Bloodshed do when played?

Savor Bloodshed sets two turn-effects when played: your next dagger attack this turn gets +4 power, and the next time you hit a marked hero with a dagger this turn, you draw a card. The +4 power is consumed by the next dagger attack. The draw effect is consumed the first time a dagger hits a marked hero that turn. It has Go again as a keyword.
What does Scar Tissue do as an Attack Reaction?

Scar Tissue (red/yellow/blue) targets a dagger attack and gives it +3/+2/+1 power. It also adds the condition 'when this hits a hero, mark them' to that dagger attack for the current combat chain. The mark effect fires on hit of the buffed dagger. This allows you to mark the hero mid-chain, enabling subsequent stealth attacks to benefit from Arakni's marked-hero bonuses.
What does To the Point do for dagger attacks versus a marked hero?

To the Point is an Attack Reaction. Its base bonus to a dagger attack is +3/+2/+1 power (red/yellow/blue). However, if the defending hero is marked when To the Point resolves, the bonus is instead +4/+3/+2 power — one more than the base. This is checked at the time To the Point resolves on the stack, so if the hero was just marked by an earlier on-hit effect this turn, To the Point gives the enhanced bonus.
What does Spreading Plague do and when is it played?

Spreading Plague is an Attack Reaction. When played, it creates a number of Bloodrot Pox tokens under the defending hero's control equal to the number of cards defending the current attack. For example, if the defending hero played 2 cards to block, 2 Bloodrot Pox tokens are created under their control. If no cards are defending, no tokens are created.
What does the Orbweaver Spinneret action do?

When you play Orbweaver Spinneret (red/yellow/blue), you equip a Graphene Chelicera token weapon to your weapon zone and your next stealth attack this turn gets +3/+2/+1 power. The Graphene Chelicera is a dagger weapon token that gives stealth daggers attacking a marked hero go again (this effect is applied by the dagger-buff listener). The power bonus from Spinneret is consumed by the next stealth attack.
What does Flick Knives do as an Attack Reaction?

Flick Knives is a once-per-turn Attack Reaction that costs 0. When played, you choose a dagger you control that is not on the active chain link, and that dagger deals 1 damage to the defending hero. If damage is dealt, that dagger is considered to have 'hit' and its on-hit triggers fire. The chosen dagger is then destroyed. This can activate hit-triggered effects on off-chain daggers mid-combat.
What does Cut from the Same Cloth do?

Cut from the Same Cloth targets the opposing hero: they reveal their hand. If any Attack Reaction card is revealed, they are marked. Your next dagger attack this turn also gets +4/+3/+2 power (red/yellow/blue). The mark and the power bonus are both applied when Cut from the Same Cloth resolves. The power bonus is set as a turn-effect consumed by the next dagger attack.
What does Take Up the Mantle do to a stealth attack targeting a marked hero?

Take Up the Mantle is an Attack Reaction. Against a non-marked defending hero, it gives a stealth attack action +2 power. Against a marked defending hero, it gives +3 power and you may banish a stealth attack action card from your graveyard. If you do, the target attack card becomes a copy of the banished card — taking its name, power, keywords, and types. This allows powerful copies of powerful stealth attacks.
What does Shred do as an Attack Reaction?

Shred targets a defending card in the current combat chain and reduces its defense value by 4/3/2 (red/yellow/blue) for the remainder of that combat chain. It can only target cards defending an Assassin attack. If there are no defending cards, Shred cannot be played. This debuffs blockers mid-combat, effectively reducing the total defense the opponent can muster.
What does Tarantula Toxin do and what are its two modes?

Tarantula Toxin is an Attack Reaction with 'Choose 1 or both:' First, if the current attack is a Dagger, it can give that dagger attack +3 power. Second, if the current attack has Stealth and there are defending cards, it can give a defending card -3 defense. If both conditions are met, you can choose to apply both effects simultaneously. If only one condition applies, you automatically get that mode.
What does Stains of the Redback do?

Stains of the Redback is an Attack Reaction (red/yellow/blue). It targets an attack with Stealth and gives it +3/+2/+1 power and go again. If the defending hero is marked, Stains costs 1 resource less to play. The power bonus and go again are both applied to the stealth attack when the reaction resolves. This is a key combo piece for powering up stealth attacks.
What does Death Touch do on hit?

Death Touch cannot be played from hand — it is only played through other means (like from a banished zone via Trap Door). When it hits, you create either a Frailty, Inertia, or Bloodrot Pox token under your opponent's control — you choose which. This is a powerful on-hit effect that can lock down the opponent with a debuff token of your choosing.
What does the Graphene Chelicera token weapon do?

Graphene Chelicera is a dagger weapon token created by Orbweaver Spinneret. It participates in the dagger-buff system: when a stealth dagger attack (a card with both Stealth and Dagger in its types) targets a marked hero, it gains go again. This conditional go again is checked when Graphene Chelicera's attacking listener fires. The effect is applied to the attacking dagger, not to the Chelicera itself.
What does Lair of the Spider do when it defends a go-again attack?

Lair of the Spider is a trap card. When it defends an attack that has go again, it marks the attacking hero. This fires when Lair of the Spider is placed as a defender and the attack has the go again keyword. The mark effect synergizes with Arakni's kit — the now-marked attacker becomes vulnerable to all of Arakni's marked-hero bonus effects on the next attack.
What does Frailty Trap do when it defends a go-again attack?

Frailty Trap creates a Frailty token under the attacking hero's control when it defends an attack that has go again. This punishes the attacker for having go again — their arsenal and weapon attacks will have -1 power from the Frailty token until it is destroyed at the attacking hero's end phase. Like Lair of the Spider, this fires when the card defends an attack with the go again keyword.
What does Inertia Trap do when it defends?

Inertia Trap creates an Inertia token under the attacking hero's control when it defends an attack whose current power exceeds that attack's base power. The condition checks if state.combat.attack_power is greater than the attack card's base_power — meaning the attack has been buffed by effects. This punishes attackers for buffing their attacks. The Inertia token forces them to bottom-deck their hand and arsenal at the start of their end phase.
What is the Instil_to_Injury (Insult to Injury) card and its effect?

Insult to Injury is a Reviled Brute Action Attack. When it attacks a hero, if you have more life than the defending hero, it gains go again. This check fires on the 'attacking' event. If the condition is met, go again is added to the combat keywords, granting an action point on resolution. This is a crowd-themed synergy card rewarding players who are winning in life total.
What does Mocking Blow do when you've been booed?

Mocking Blow first checks if you have more life than the defending hero — if so, the crowd boos you. Then, if you have been booed this turn (from any source, including this trigger), Mocking Blow gains +4/+3/+2 power (red/yellow/blue). The boo and the power check happen on the 'attacking' event in sequence: the boo fires, then the has_been_booed flag is checked and power is applied.
What does Show of Strength do when cards with 6+ power defend it?

Show of Strength is an attack that has a continuous penalty when defended: it loses 1 power for each defending card that has 6 or more power. The penalty fires on the 'defend' event and applies to the current attack power immediately. For example, if two 6+ power cards block Show of Strength, it loses 2 power. This makes it weaker against large blockers.
What does Snarky Prick do when it attacks?

When Snarky Prick attacks a hero, it looks at the top card of the defending hero's deck. If that card is red (pitch value 1), the top card is destroyed (sent to graveyard) and Snarky Prick gets +4 power. If the top card is not red, nothing additional happens. The card is not revealed to the opponent before the check — the condition is evaluated on the card's pitch value directly.
What does Swing Big do if it doesn't hit?

If Swing Big does not hit the defending hero (the attack is fully blocked), when the combat chain closes, the defending hero creates a Quicken token. This is a combat chain close trigger that checks the chain link record for Swing Big to see if it hit. If it did not hit, the Quicken token is created under the defending hero's control — rewarding successful defense.
What does Nimblism (blue) do when played?

The blue Nimblism sets a turn-effect so the next attack action card with cost 1 or less that you play this turn gets +1 power. This is a small buff targeted at low-cost attacks. The flag 'nimblism_next_attack_plus1' is consumed by the next qualifying attack action played that turn. The TURN_ATTACK_EFFECTS registry checks cost <= 1 before applying the bonus.
What does Nimby do when it attacks?

When Nimby attacks, you may search your deck for a Nimblism card, reveal it, and put it into your hand, then shuffle your deck. The search is optional — you can choose not to search, and if you do search you may 'fail to find' even if a Nimblism exists in the deck. The shuffle always happens regardless of whether a card was found or the search was initiated.
What does Offensive Behavior do on attack and on hit?

Offensive Behavior has two effects. First, a continuous ability on attack: if you control a Might or Vigor token, it gets +1 power. Second, an on-hit effect: when it hits a hero, you create both a Might token and a Vigor token. The on-attack check fires first (using existing tokens), and the token creation fires after a successful hit, providing a snowballing effect as tokens accumulate.
What is the Apex Bonebreaker's triggered effect when defending?

When Apex Bonebreaker defends alongside a card that has 6 or more power (in the same combat chain's defending cards), you create a Might token. The condition checks all other defending cards in the current combat chain — if any other card defending with Apex Bonebreaker has power >= 6, the Might token is created. Apex Bonebreaker itself is excluded from the check.
What does Overcrowded do when it attacks or defends?

Overcrowded has the Ambush keyword and gains bonuses based on the number of unique aura token names in the arena (across both players). When it attacks, it gets +1 power per unique token name. When it defends, it gets +1 defense per unique token name. The count checks all aura tokens in the arena at the time the trigger fires, making it stronger the more diverse the token board state is.
What does Reckless Arithmetic do when it attacks?

When Reckless Arithmetic attacks, the controller rolls a 6-sided die and adds the result to the attack's power. The die result is entirely random (1-6), so Reckless Arithmetic's power ranges from its base power + 1 to base power + 6. The engine uses roll_die() which generates a random integer in that range.
What does Pummel do as an Attack Reaction and what are its two modes?

Pummel has two modes. Mode 1: if the current attack is from a Club or Hammer weapon, give it +4 power. Mode 2: if the current attack is an attack action card with cost 2 or more, give it +4 power and add an on-hit discard effect (the defending hero discards a card if this attack hits). If only one mode is valid, it is applied automatically. If both are valid, you choose. If neither is valid, Pummel cannot be played.
What does Sink Below do as a defense reaction?

Sink Below is a defense reaction. When played, you may put a card from your hand on the bottom of your deck. If you do, draw a card. This is optional — you can play Sink Below as a 3-defense blocker without activating the hand-filtering effect. If you choose to bottom-deck a card, you immediately draw a replacement, making it a net-neutral card draw while also providing defense.
What does Cloud Cover (red) do as a damage prevention instant?

Cloud Cover (red, pitch 1) sets a one-shot damage prevention replacement effect for the next time you would be dealt damage this turn: prevent 3 of that damage. The yellow version prevents 2 and the blue version prevents 1. The prevention is applied as a replacement effect that fires on the next incoming damage event targeting you. After the first damage event is modified, the replacement effect is consumed.
What does Throw Caution to the Wind do?

Throw Caution to the Wind reveals the top card of your deck (makes it public). The next time you would be dealt damage this turn, prevent X of that damage where X equals the pitch value of the revealed card (1 for red, 2 for yellow, 3 for blue). This is a one-shot prevention replacement effect. If the deck is empty, there is no revealed card and no prevention.
What does Three of a Kind do when played?

Three of a Kind draws 3 cards and then until end of turn, you may only play cards from your arsenal. The arsenal-only restriction is tracked by the 'play_from_arsenal_only' flag and the engine enforces it when determining legal plays. This dramatically limits your options after playing Three of a Kind — you can only use what you had stored in your arsenal for the rest of that turn.
What does Sift do when played?

Sift lets you put up to 4 cards from your hand on the bottom of your deck in any order (choosing them one at a time), then draw that many cards. If you bottom-deck 3 cards, you draw 3. This is a powerful hand-filter that lets you cycle bad cards for new ones. You can stop early by choosing 'done' and draw fewer cards if you prefer to keep more of your hand.
What does Portside Exchange do when played?

Portside Exchange lets you choose a card from your hand to discard, then you draw a card. If the discarded card was yellow (pitch value 2), you also create a Gold token. This is a hand-filter that rewards discarding yellow cards by generating Gold. The Gold creation fires only if the specifically chosen card had pitch value 2.
What does Sea Floor Salvage do?

Sea Floor Salvage targets any face-up card in either player's graveyard and turns it face-down. If that card was yellow (pitch value 2), you create a Gold token. This hides information about the graveyard and generates Gold for yellow cards. It can target any player's graveyard, not just your own.
What does Sunken Treasure do when it defends?

When Sunken Treasure defends, you may choose a face-up card in either player's graveyard and turn it face-down. If that card was yellow, create a Gold token. This is an optional triggered ability — you can decline. Like Sea Floor Salvage, this hides graveyard information and rewards yellow-card targeting with Gold. The effect fires when Sunken Treasure joins the defenders.
What does Gold the Tip do?

Gold the Tip is a Pirate action. When played, your next arrow attack this turn gets +3 power. Additionally, if you have a face-up yellow arrow in your arsenal, you create a Gold token immediately on play. The +3 power is stored as a turn-effect consumed by the next arrow attack. The Gold creation is a conditional bonus checking the arsenal content at the time of play.
What does Murderous Rabble do when it attacks?

When Murderous Rabble attacks, it reveals the top card of your deck (makes it public) and adds power equal to that card's pitch value. Red top card (pitch 1) gives +1 power, yellow gives +2, blue gives +3. The top card stays on top of the deck after the reveal — it is not drawn or moved. This makes Murderous Rabble's effective power range from base +1 to base +3.
What does Battering Bolt do on hit?

When Battering Bolt hits a hero, the defending hero reveals their hand, all non-action cards in their hand are discarded, and they lose 1 life for each card discarded this way. This can strip the opponent's hand of equipment, instants, and other non-action cards while dealing bonus life loss. Action cards in the hand are safe from this discard.
What does Shallow Water Shark Harpoon do if the Hammerhead Cannon was activated this turn?

If the Hammerhead Harpoon Cannon was activated this turn ('activated_cannon' flag), Shallow Water Shark Harpoon gains 'on hit: choose a card in the defending hero's arsenal to destroy, then create a Gold token.' This on-hit effect only applies if the cannon was activated. Without cannon activation, Shallow Water Shark Harpoon is a standard arrow/harpoon attack.
What does Big Game Trophy Shot do when played?

Big Game Trophy Shot sets 'next arrow attack this turn gets +4 power.' Additionally, if that next arrow attack has 'harpoon' in its name, that harpoon gains 'when this hits a hero, create a Gold token.' Big Game Trophy Shot also draws a card then discards a card, and has Go again. This is a powerful setup card for harpoon-heavy turns.
What does Catch of the Day do when played?

Catch of the Day gives your next arrow attack this turn +2 power and makes Go Fish triggers fire twice this turn. The double-Go Fish flag ('go_fish_double') allows harpoon hits to trigger their hand-reveal effect twice. This doubles the pressure on the defending hero's hand when a harpoon hits. Catch of the Day also has Go again as a keyword.
What does Marlynn's hero ability do?

Marlynn, Treasure Hunter has an Action ability. The cost is tapping her hero card and destroying a Gold token you control. The effect is creating a Goldfin Harpoon (yellow) in your hand and gaining Go again (an action point). This allows Marlynn to generate harpoon arrows mid-turn if she has Gold tokens to spend, enabling sustained harpoon pressure.
What does Gold-Baited Hook do when activated and when does it get destroyed?

Activating Gold-Baited Hook (Instant, tap cost) sets a flag: the next Pirate attack you make this turn gets an on-hit effect to steal or create a Gold token. Go again is also granted. At the start of your end phase, if the hook was activated this turn but no Gold was obtained (either by the on-hit steal/create or by any other Gold creation during the activation window), the hook is destroyed. If any Gold was obtained, the hook survives.
What does the Quiver of Abyssal Depths activation do?

Activating Quiver of Abyssal Depths (cost: 3 resources and destroy this) lets you shuffle up to 3 arrows with different names from your graveyard back into your deck, then shuffle the deck. This recovers spent arrows, including harpoons, for reuse. The quiver is destroyed as part of the cost, so it is a one-time use per equip. You select up to 3 arrows of different names, not just any 3 arrows.
What does Old Knocker do when activated?

Old Knocker is a Chest Equipment with an activation ability. The cost is tapping your hero and destroying Old Knocker itself. The effect is gaining 1 resource. This is an expensive activation — you sacrifice a chest equipment slot and tap your hero for a single resource. It is designed as an emergency resource generator when you need exactly 1 more resource to play a key card.
What does Sealace Sarong do when activated?

Sealace Sarong has an Instant activation (tap cost). Activation condition: you must have a blue arrow in your arsenal (face-up or face-down with blue pitch). The effect turns the blue arrow in your arsenal face-up and gives it go again this turn. This allows you to play the arsenal arrow immediately (as its face-up status makes it playable) and the go again lets you continue the combat chain after playing it.
What does Temporal Wobble do as an instant?

Temporal Wobble can negate a target non-attack action card on the stack if that card's cost is less than the number of Sigil auras you control. You choose a valid target from the stack, and it is negated (removed from the stack without resolving). Regardless of whether a target is found and negated, the opposing hero gains an action point. This is a conditional counterspell that scales with your Sigil count.
What does Electromagnetic Somersault do?

Electromagnetic Somersault returns up to 2 attack action cards from the active chain link to their owner's hand, but only cards that meet a minimum cost threshold. The red version (pitch 1) targets attack action cards with cost 1 or more; the blue version (pitch 3) targets attack action cards with cost 2 or more. Free (cost 0) attack action cards cannot be targeted by either version. This includes the current attacking card and any qualifying attack action cards used to defend on the current chain link. Returning a card from the combat chain removes it from the chain, reducing the attacker's offense or the defender's defense mid-combat. You choose which eligible cards to return (up to 2).
What does Comet Storm Shock (meld) do?

Comet Storm Shock is a meld card. When played, it deals 5 arcane damage to the opponent. This is a high-value arcane damage spell in Oscilio's meld arsenal. The meld mechanic (handled by the engine) involves combining two cards to play the meld form — Comet Storm and Shock are melded together to produce the Comet Storm Shock effect.
What does Null Shock (meld) do and what is its condition?

Null Shock is a meld card. When played, it negates a target instant card on the stack if that instant's cost is less than the total arcane damage dealt this turn by the controller. The arcane damage count is tracked via 'dealt_arcane' entries in current_turn_effects. If no eligible instant is on the stack, nothing is negated. This is a conditional counter-spell that gets more powerful the more arcane damage you've dealt.
What does Consign to Cosmos Shock (meld) do?

Per card text, Consign to Cosmos Shock banishes X instant and/or aura cards from any graveyard (either player's), where X equals the total amount of arcane damage you have dealt this turn. The controller chooses which graveyard cards to banish. There are two known discrepancies between the card text and the current engine implementation: (1) the implementation only targets the opponent's graveyard, not any graveyard; (2) the implementation counts the number of arcane damage events (times arcane damage was dealt) rather than the total amount of arcane damage — so dealing 3 damage in one event counts as X=1 in the engine but should be X=3 per card text. Additionally, the 'dealt_arcane' tracking has a separate known bug where arcane damage is not appended at all, so X is always 0 in practice.
What does Aether Bindings of the Third Age's Battleworn keyword mean?

Battleworn on Aether Bindings of the Third Age means: when the combat chain closes, if this card defended during that chain, put a -1 defense counter on it. The bindings start with 1 defense, so each defend reduces their blocking value by 1. Once defense reaches 0, the bindings provide no blocking value. Battleworn does not destroy the card — it just accumulates -1 counters.
What does Scabskin Leathers do when activated?

Scabskin Leathers has an Once per Turn Action activation. When activated at cost 0, the controller rolls a 6-sided die and gains action points equal to half the die result rounded down. A roll of 1-2 gives 0 AP, a roll of 3-4 gives 1 AP, and a roll of 5-6 gives 2 AP. This is an entirely random action-point generation mechanic with no guaranteed return.
What does Kayo's hero ability do?

Kayo, Underhanded Cheat has a Once per Turn Instant ability costing 4 resources and requiring tapping his hero card. It targets an attack action card he controls and sets its base power to 6. This clears all existing power effects on the target and sets a fixed 6 base power. The targeting requires a valid attack action card controlled by Kayo to be on the combat chain or stack.
What does the Booze aura card do when it enters and leaves the arena?

Booze is an aura that booes you when it enters the arena and also boos you when it leaves the arena, for any reason. At the start of your turn, if Booze is in your aura zone, it is destroyed (which triggers the leave-boo again). This means playing Booze results in being booed immediately, and then booed again when it is destroyed at the start of your next turn. Booze has Go again as a keyword, granting an action point when played.
What is the 'the crowd boos' keyword and what does it do?

The Crowd Boos is a keyword ability printed on certain cards (like Big Bully). When a card with this keyword attacks, and the attacker has more life than the defending hero, the crowd boos the attacker. The crowd-boos event creates a game state flag ('crowd_boos' event) that other effects can listen to. Cards like Kayo Underhanded Cheat create tokens in response to being booed, and cards like Big Bully and Mocking Blow gain power bonuses based on having been booed.
What does Looking for a Scrap do as an additional cost?

Looking for a Scrap has an optional additional cost on play: you may banish a card with exactly 1 power from your graveyard. If you do, Looking for a Scrap gains +1 power and Go again. If you cannot or choose not to pay the additional cost, the card plays normally without the bonus. The additional cost is evaluated at play time from the on_play trigger.
What is the Scrap keyword and how does it work?

Scrap is an optional additional cost keyword. When you play a card with Scrap, you may banish an item or equipment card from your graveyard as an additional cost. If you do, you unlock a bonus effect specified on the card. The banish is optional — declining to pay does not prevent playing the card, it just means you miss the bonus. The choice is made when the card is played.
What does the Beat Chest keyword do?

Beat Chest is an optional additional cost keyword. When you play a card with Beat Chest, you may discard a card with 6 or more power from your hand as an additional cost. If you do, you unlock the bonus effect. If no card with 6+ power is in hand, or you choose not to discard, the card plays normally without the bonus. The engine checks for eligible 6+ power hand cards and presents the choice to the player.
What does the Heave keyword do?

Heave N is an optional triggered ability: at the beginning of your end phase, while this card is in your hand, you may pay N resources to put this card from your hand into your arsenal. This allows you to bank hand cards into your arsenal for use on future turns. The choice is optional and requires paying the resource cost each time. The trigger fires at the start of your end phase while the card remains in hand.
What does the Opt keyword do?

Opt N is an on-play triggered ability: when you play a card with Opt N, look at the top N cards of your deck, put any number on the bottom in any order, and the rest on top in any order. The engine calls effect_opt() which handles this deck-filtering action. Opt 1 means look at 1 card and keep or bottom it. Opt allows you to smooth future draws by filtering the top of your deck.
What is the Blood Debt keyword and when does it trigger?

Blood Debt is a triggered ability: at the beginning of your end phase, while this card is banished face-up, you lose 1 life. The trigger fires on the 'start_of_end_phase' event and checks if the card is in the banished zone and is public (face-up). Blood Debt punishes you each turn that the banished card remains face-up. Some cards interact with Blood Debt by turning cards face-down to prevent the life loss.
What does Watery Grave do?

Watery Grave is triggered when the card with this keyword is put into the graveyard from the arena (including from the combat chain). When this happens, the card is turned face-down in the graveyard. This hides information about what is in the graveyard, preventing opponents from seeing the card and strategically using knowledge of graveyard contents. It triggers on the 'card_destroyed' event when the previous zone was an arena zone.
What does the Suspense keyword do when a card enters the arena?

When a card with Suspense enters the arena, it enters with 2 suspense counters. At the start of each turn, one suspense counter is removed. When the last counter is removed and the count reaches 0, the card is destroyed. Suspense therefore gives a card a 2-turn lifespan in the arena (it survives through 2 start-of-turn triggers, then is destroyed on the third). This is tracked via the 'suspense' counter in the player's counters dict.
What is the Rune Gate keyword and how does it work?

Rune Gate allows you to play the card from your banished zone without paying its cost, provided you control enough Runechant tokens — specifically, as many Runechants as the card's cost. If you control the required number of Runechants, the card can be played from banish for free. This is handled by the legal_actions check in the engine (play-from-banished path), not as a trigger. The keyword allows repeated use of powerful cards from the banish zone in Runeblade strategies.
What is the Crank keyword and when does it fire?

Crank is a triggered ability that fires when the card enters the arena (the 'enters_arena' event). The crank() effect puts a +1 counter of some kind on a Mechanologist item or equipment. This is optional — the player is prompted to choose whether to crank and which target (depending on the card's specific crank text). Crank is the Mechanologist mechanic for building up items via counters.
What is the Boost keyword and when does it trigger?

Boost is an optional ability that fires on the 'on_play' event when a card with Boost is played. The player may optionally reveal the top card of their deck. If the revealed card is a Mechanologist card, it is put into play (typically triggering its own enters-arena effects). Boost allows Mechanologist players to chain items and equipment into play from the top of the deck. The choice is optional — you can decline and the top card stays hidden.
What is Dominate and how does it affect blocking?

Dominate is a static keyword. While an attack with Dominate is on the combat chain, the defending hero can block with at most 1 card from their hand. Cards from the arsenal can still be used in addition, and equipment can still be used passively. The engine checks this via dominate_check(), which counts hand-originated defending cards and prevents adding a second hand card if one is already defending.
What is Overpower and how does it affect blocking?

Overpower is a static keyword. While an attack with Overpower is on the combat chain, the defending hero can block with at most 1 action card. This prevents multi-action-card blocks. Non-action cards (like defense reactions from hand) may still be played alongside. The engine checks via overpower_check() which counts defending cards that have 'Action' in their types.
What is Phantasm and what causes a Phantasm card to be destroyed?

Phantasm is a triggered ability. When a non-Illusionist attack action card with 6 or more power is played to defend a Phantasm attack, the Phantasm attack is destroyed. The trigger fires on the 'defend' event and checks if any non-Illusionist attacking action card with power >= 6 is among the defenders. This makes Phantasm attacks fragile against large non-Illusionist blockers.
What is Spectra and what triggers its destruction?

Spectra is a triggered ability: when a card with Spectra becomes the target of an attack, it is destroyed. The trigger fires on the 'target_of_attack' event. This means Spectra cards (typically auras or allies) cannot be attacked directly — attempting to target them destroys them before damage resolves. Spectra makes certain permanents immune to direct attacks by auto-destroying on being targeted.
What is Crush and when does a Crush effect trigger?

Crush is a label keyword. A Crush effect triggers when the attack deals 4 or more damage. The trigger fires on the 'damage_dealt' event and checks via crush_check() whether the damage amount was 4 or more. The specific Crush effect varies per card — each card defines what happens when the Crush threshold is met. Crush checks the actual damage dealt after prevention, not the attack power.
What is the Reprise keyword and when does it trigger?

Reprise is a label keyword that fires when you play a Reprise card and the defending hero has previously defended from their hand during this combat chain. The trigger checks via reprise_check() whether any card from the defending hero's hand was already played to defend this chain. If the defending hero has not defended from hand yet, Reprise does not trigger even if Reprise is on the card.
What is Rupture and when does a Rupture effect trigger?

Rupture is a label keyword. A Rupture effect triggers when the card is played at chain link 4 or higher. The trigger checks via rupture_check() whether the current chain link number is 4 or more. This encourages long combat chains — cards with Rupture become significantly more powerful later in a chain. The chain link count is tracked in the game state.
What is a Combo keyword and when does it trigger?

Combo is a label keyword that triggers when a specified named card was the last attack action card played in the combat chain before the Combo card. The engine checks via combo_check() using a list of card names that satisfy the combo condition. If the previous attack matches one of the named cards, the Combo effect fires. This creates two-card attack combos for Ninja and other class strategies.
What is Surge and when does a Surge effect trigger?

Surge is a label keyword. A Surge effect triggers when the attack or action deals more than a specified number of damage — the exact threshold is printed on the card. The trigger fires on the 'damage_dealt' event and checks via surge_check(event, threshold) whether the damage meets the condition. For example, 'Surge — if this deals more than 2 damage' means the Surge fires at 3 or more damage dealt.
What is Galvanize and how does it affect Lightning cards played after it?

Galvanize is a keyword that grants Amp 1 whenever a Lightning card is played after the Galvanize card this turn. The galvanize() effect registers a listener for subsequent Lightning card plays and applies Amp to each one. This creates a chain of amplification — each subsequent Lightning card played benefits from the Galvanize that was set up earlier in the turn.
What is the Legendary keyword on equipment and resource cards?

Legendary means you can include only 1 copy of this card in your deck. For equipment, it also typically means you can only have one equipped at a time per slot. Cards like Schism of Chaos and Riches of Trōpal-Dhani have Legendary, limiting deck construction to a single copy. The Legendary restriction is a deck-building rule enforced at construction time, not a game-play trigger.
What is the 'once per turn' restriction on hero abilities, and can it be reset?

Hero abilities marked 'Once per Turn' can only be used once per turn cycle. In the engine, this is tracked via flags like 'oscilio_used' or 'volzar_used' in the player's current_turn_effects list. The flag prevents re-activation. These flags are cleared at the start of a new turn when current_turn_effects is reset. Unless a card effect specifically resets the once-per-turn counter mid-turn, the ability cannot be reused.
When does an on-hit trigger fire relative to other effects?

On-hit triggers fire on the 'hit' event, which occurs after an attack resolves and deals at least 1 damage to the defending hero. The sequence is: attack resolves, damage is calculated and dealt, the 'damage_dealt' event fires (for Crush/Surge checks), then if damage was dealt to the hero the 'hit' event fires. On-hit triggers are stacked on the event queue and resolve in registration order, with players receiving priority between trigger resolutions per the rules.
What is the difference between 'on play' and 'enters the arena' events in the engine?

The 'on_play' event fires when a card is placed on the stack to be played — this covers action cards, instants, and auras when they are declared played. The 'enters_arena' event fires when a permanent card (equipment, aura, ally, item) actually moves into an arena zone, which for auras happens when the on_play resolves and the card transitions to the aura zone. Crown of Dominion uses 'enters_arena' because its effect fires on equipment entering the slot, not on card declaration.
